author: Forbes
description:
Thousands of children lost a parent in the deadly attacks on September 11, 2001, and hundreds of those kids were the kids of first responders who lost their lives trying to help the public on that deadly day. In the wake of the tragedy, The First Responders Children's Foundation was created to support these children. FRCF CEO Jillian Crane joined Forbes' Maggie McGrath to reflect on the 25th anniversary of 9/11 and to talk about the ways the FRCF has evolved to help the families of any active duty first responder or a first responder who has lost their life helping the public.

description:
Economic security can be a critical pathway to safety for survivors of domestic violence. In this powerful conversation, Kate Nack, The Allstate Foundation and Social Impact Vice President explains how employers can support survivors through financial resources, flexibility, paid leave and compassionate workplace policies.

The message is simple: safe workplaces save lives—and financial independence can give survivors the power and freedom to build a future without fear.

author: Forbes
description:
On September 11, 2001, Lauren Manning was heading to her office at Cantor Fitzgerald in the North Tower when American Airlines Flight 11 struck the building.

Burned over 82.5% of her body and facing devastating injuries and the loss of 658 colleagues, Manning made a choice: to live.

Twenty-five years later, the 9/11 survivor, author and founder of Narrative Mind Works reflects on survival, grief, motherhood and resilience—and the power of choosing how we move forward after adversity.

“Every day you have a choice. Make it count.”
